Just discovered this gem at my local Dollar Tree, I used it earlier to clean some stains on the upholstery of my car seat and even on the wheel of my car. I couldn't be happier with the result. It's possibly my favorite all purpose cleaner now.

Is there any legitimate reason I shouldn't use this product? The dollar price point is super attractive, but it makes me concerned that the manufacturer may be cutting some corners. Is anyone knowledgable on it willing to weigh in? Until someone says otherwise, I think I've found my new go to for cleaning, degreasing, and stain removal.
For those who might be interested, here's a link to the product on the Dollar Tree website: http://dollartree.com/mt/www.dollartree.com/20-oz-Totally-Awesome-Cleaner/p8056/index.pro

When I first tried it, I was skeptical. I thought "these assholes literally named their crap product 'awesome' to trick me," and decided I hated everyone involved with the product. I bought it anyway because I really needed some kind of cleaner, and also, despite hating them all, I had a certain respect for an asshole with the balls to literally call their product "Awesome" outright like that.

I was an idiot. Now I only get Awesome. I'm like a walking commercial for the shit. I haven't had any problems with it. I think they can sell for $1 because 1.) I've never in my life seen one single advertisement for the product- leading me to believe they just cut out advertising altogether 2.) most cleaning agent companies could probably turn a profit selling their product for a dollar if they cut out a lot of the brand name fat, and 3.) they don't have a thousand and a half scents and products in all their various bottles. They have a few products, they have like, 2 scents, and that's it.

I guess the spray on the bottles aren't always that great on the spray bottles. The plastic on the container is a little thin. I get the refill bottles anyway, without a spray top on them. Just buy a better bottle, if it really comes down to it, and you'll never have that problem again. As long as I've been using it (and it's been about 5 years now that I've stuck with it) I haven't found the actual cleaning agent itself lacking in quality. I think the corners they're cutting are something I'd rather most companies cut.
Oh yeah, those spray bottles break easily. Definitely better to use a different bottle.

Well, it has a vaguely chemical smell (ethanol maybe?) with possibly a hint of lemon. its fairly mild, but I still try not to breathe it in. It makes me cough a little if it's too concentrated in a small space. I definitely wouldn't use it to try and freshen up my house.

I think that they do make an orange version, but I haven't tried it yet. Maybe someone else has some experience?
Wow, a lot more depth than I was thinking in that reply. I was looking for something along the lines of "it smells like oranges or lemons." Bravo.

I'd swear the smell is ammonia, even though the label says there isn't any. When using it to clean nicotine off walls, or soap scum off shower walls, don't spray it as the irritant contacts lots of air that way. Saturate your scrub pad or whatever and use that. If it's a huge area, I hold the open bottle against the wall so it's almost sealed, but a bit drips out, then quickly swipe the rivulets out across the wall before it gets to the bottom.
I cannot reccomend this stuff highly enough. It cleans anything!

I live in an apartment with a fairly small kitchen/dining room floor. I use the orange version to manually scrub my laminated wood floors (with paper towels). Works so much better than mops, which just seem to spread the dirt around. I can tell how well it's working by looking at the paper towels afterwawrd. After the first cleaning, the towels were black. (Yuck!) Next cleaning they were dark grey. Now that the floor is clean to start with, the towels just turn light grey with each cleaning.
Paper towels are good. Personally I use an old swiffer mop head and a ratty old washcloth soaked in the Totally Awesome Orange product. No more greasy floor in front of the stove :0)

Love this stuff! I have a cleaning business, and when I'm low on degreaser, I'll stop by Dollar General and get this if I don't have time to restock at the office.

Another option, if you have a Sam's membership, is Pro-force degreaser. You can get a gallon of concentrate for $7, and it makes 120 bottles or so of cleaner - look for the purple stuff. This is what we normally use, and it is amazing! If I have a tough job, I just make the degreaser a little stronger. You only need about an ounce or so per bottle of cleaner, no more than 3 ounces of concentrate to 20 oz. water in most cases.

Comparing msds of Totally Awesome and Pro-force, they're both fairly safe and highly alkaline (pH 12-13). Man, I wish I could find Totally Awesome in a concentrated form!
Been very happy with all the Totally Awesome stuff. As someone else mentioned their spray bottles are flimsy so transfer liquids to a better one if possible.
